# Subagent routing

Delegate to a specialized subagent (Agent tool) whenever a request matches one of
these triggers, instead of doing the work in the main conversation. Delegation keeps
verbose output out of this context and applies the agent's checklist and report
format. Do small, obvious edits yourself. Name the agent when the user does.

- `claude-api-reviewer` (Reviews code calling the Claude API, Anthropic SDKs or Agent SDK): Use when reviewing such code or diagnosing 400s, truncation or cache misses from source.
- `claude-md-curator` (Creates or maintains CLAUDE.md files): Use when a repo needs a verified CLAUDE.md (e.g. after /init) or its memory is stale or bloated.
- `llm-eval-designer` (Designs and builds evals for LLM features): Use when measuring LLM output quality, comparing prompts/models on your data, or gating prompt/model changes.
- `mcp-server-builder` (Builds, extends or fixes Model Context Protocol): Use when creating an MCP server or changing its tools, transport or auth.
- `prompt-engineer` (Writes and improves prompts for LLM features in application code): Use when an LLM feature returns wrong, inconsistent or unparseable output, or needs a new prompt.
- `subagent-auditor` (Audits subagent definitions): Use when reviewing an agent library or finding which descriptions collide.
- `subagent-author` (Creates or improves Claude Code subagent files): Use when adding an agent or fixing a named one that misroutes or misbehaves.
- `code-simplifier` (Behavior-preserving refactoring of recently changed or named code): Use when working code should be cleaned up or simplified without changing behavior.
- `dependency-upgrader` (Upgrades a library, framework, runtime or SDK across major): Use when bumping a dependency or runtime version, applying dependency-auditor fixes, or assessing an upgrade.
- `dotnet-modernizer` (Ports .NET Framework apps to modern .NET project by project): Use when assessing, planning or doing a .NET Framework 4.x move to .NET 8+/.NET Core.
- `legacy-code-analyst` (Extracts and documents business rules, data flows, dependencies, side effects of legacy code): Use when asked what old code does or before a rewrite, migration or characterization tests.
- `manufacturing-integration-engineer` (Designs and reviews ISA-95 Level 2-4 integrations): Use when designing or reviewing a SCADA, plant-floor or MES interface.
- `change-control-impact-assessor` (Drafts a GxP change-control impact assessment): Use when a change needs a change control record or revalidation call.
- `csv-validation-author` (Drafts GxP computer system validation): Use when QA needs a validation package, RTM or IQ/OQ/PQ.
- `gxp-data-integrity-reviewer` (Reviews data integrity of GxP-regulated code): Use PROACTIVELY after changes to such code.
- `data-analyst` (Answers questions from data files): Use when asked to analyze or answer a question from a dataset.
- `database-architect` (Designs new database schemas or major restructurings, or critiques an existing schema's design): Use when modelling new data or reshaping tables.
- `migration-reviewer` (Reviews database schema migrations): Use when a change adds or edits migration files, or before one runs on production data.
- `sql-query-tuner` (Tunes slow SQL): Use when a specific query or procedure is slow.
- `build-fixer` (Gets a failing build, compile, type-check, lint or dependency restore green with the smallest correct diff): Use PROACTIVELY after an edit or merge breaks the build.
- `ci-failure-investigator` (Diagnoses a failed CI run): Use when a pipeline, PR check or CI test is red.
- `debugger` (Root-causes and fixes bugs that fail every run): Use PROACTIVELY when a test fails or code throws or misbehaves at runtime.
- `git-bisector` (Finds the commit that introduced a regression with `git bisect run` from a good ref, a bad ref): Use when asked which commit broke or slowed something that worked in a known earlier version.
- `log-analyzer` (Digests large logs, traces and exports): Use when a log is too big to read raw or to learn from logs when and why an incident started.
- `performance-analyst` (Finds and measures performance bottlenecks): Use when working code is too slow.
- `bash-scripter` (Writes, reviews and hardens shell scripts): Use when creating, fixing or reviewing a shell script, or a script fails with 'unbound variable'/'command not found'.
- `ci-pipeline-engineer` (Writes and fixes CI/CD pipeline YAML for GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines and GitLab CI): Use when creating, changing or hardening a pipeline.
- `container-engineer` (Writes and optimizes Dockerfiles, .dockerignore and docker-compose files): Use when containerizing an app or fixing a slow, bloated, insecure or failing image or compose setup.
- `iac-reviewer` (Reviews infrastructure-as-code and deployment config): Use when reviewing infra code or changes for misconfigurations before apply or deploy.
- `observability-engineer` (Adds or improves observability in application code): Use when adding logging, metrics, tracing, health checks or alerts to a service.
- `powershell-scripter` (Writes, reviews and fixes PowerShell scripts and modules): Use when creating, fixing or reviewing PowerShell, including AD, Azure or Exchange admin scripts.
- `adr-writer` (Records an architecture decision as an ADR in the repo's template or MADR): Use when a decision already made or proposed needs writing down.
- `clueless-reader` (Deliberately clueless literal reader): Use when testing whether a README, runbook, setup guide, prompt or skill can be followed with zero background knowledge, or for trivial read-and-report tasks.
- `diagram-generator` (Generates Mermaid diagrams from the actual code): Use when asked to draw, diagram or visualize existing code or flows.
- `docs-sync-editor` (Fixes docs that are out of date after a code change, with minimal edits): Use when code changed and docs must catch up.
- `technical-writer` (Writes new docs): Use when a doc or section does not exist or needs a rewrite, including for new features.
- `changelog-writer` (Updates CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section from commits/PRs since the last tag): Use when the changelog lags merged work.
- `git-historian` (Answers why code is the way it is from version control): Use when asking why, when or by whom code changed.
- `merge-conflict-resolver` (Resolves git merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert and stash-pop conflicts by combining the intent of both...): Use when git reports conflicts or conflict markers remain.
- `pr-description-writer` (Drafts a pull request): Use when opening or updating a PR.
- `i18n-engineer` (Internationalizes apps): Use when adding a locale, auditing i18n, or fixing locale display bugs (date off by a day, wrong decimal separator).
- `requirements-analyst` (Turns a vague request, ticket, email or meeting note into testable, code-grounded requirements for new or...): Use when asked for requirements, acceptance criteria, a PRD or URS.
- `docs-researcher` (Answers how-to, config and API-deprecation questions on a library, framework, SDK, CLI or cloud service...): Use when an answer must be checked against current docs for the version in use or cited.
- `feature-tracer` (Explains how an existing feature works end to end): Use to trace, file by file, what happens when it runs.
- `library-evaluator` (Compares candidate libraries, frameworks or services): Use when choosing what to adopt or replace.
- `accessibility-reviewer` (WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility): Use when an accessibility, WCAG, Section 508 or screen-reader review is requested.
- `api-contract-reviewer` (Reviews API contracts): Use when routes, DTOs or schemas change, or before publishing an API.
- `architecture-reviewer` (Reviews structure of a change or code area): Use when adding modules/services/integrations, after big refactors, or for "is this the right design?".
- `code-reviewer` (Reviews the current change): Use PROACTIVELY after editing code, before commit or PR.
- `concurrency-reviewer` (Reviews code for race conditions, thread-safety, deadlocks, lost DB updates and async/goroutine leaks): Use when code shares state across threads, tasks or requests.
- `dependency-auditor` (Audits dependencies via manifests, lockfiles and native tools): Use when asked which packages have CVEs or are stale.
- `finding-verifier` (Dispatched with ONE reported finding): Use when a reviewer's or scanner's claim must be confirmed before acting; not for general requests.
- `security-reviewer` (Security review of changed code or named paths): Use PROACTIVELY before committing changes to auth, user input, SQL/shell/file/network calls, deserialization, crypto, secrets, sessions/tokens, uploads, redirects or templates.
- `silent-failure-hunter` (Finds swallowed exceptions and silent failures in a diff or named paths): Use when errors vanish or before merging error handling.
- `spec-compliance-reviewer` (Checks an implementation): Use when asked whether a change matches the ticket, spec or plan.
- `change-verifier` (Independently proves a claimed fix or feature works by running it): Use PROACTIVELY before declaring a non-trivial fix or feature done, or when asked to confirm a change really works.
- `e2e-test-writer` (Writes browser end-to-end tests): Use when asked for E2E, UI, smoke or browser tests of a user journey.
- `flaky-test-investigator` (Diagnoses intermittent): Use when a test passes and fails without code changes or only sometimes in CI.
- `release-readiness-gate` (Go/no-go gate before tagging or deploying a release): Use when asked if a release is ready to ship.
- `test-gap-analyzer` (Finds what is NOT tested in the current diff or named modules, ranked by risk): Use when asking what tests are missing or whether a change is adequately tested.
- `test-runner` (Runs the project's tests): Use PROACTIVELY after code edits for a mid-task pass/fail check, or when asked to run tests.
- `test-writer` (Writes unit, component and integration tests for named code or the current diff in the repo's existing...): Use when tests need to be added, extended or updated for a change.
